standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the characterising relation for the classes obtained by capping with the Chern classes, and the uniqueness identifying the classes obtained after applying the Gysin map.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Gysin map factors through rational equivalence, commutes with the cap with a first Chern class and with flat pullback
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels lemma-gysin-factors (proof line 7514), lemma-gysin-commutes-cap-c1 (proof line 7516) and lemma-gysin-flat-pullback (proof line 7517)
standard_prerequisites.use: They allow the Gysin map to be applied to the relation and the result rewritten in terms of the Gysin images of the classes.

core_obligations: Record the relation: write the classes obtained by capping with the Chern classes of the bundle and their characterising relation on the projective bundle of the bundle (proof lines 7495-7504).

Apply the Gysin map: form the fibre product diagram of the projective bundle of the restricted bundle, note that the twisting sheaf is pulled back, apply the Gysin map to the relation, and use its compatibility with the cap with a first Chern class and with flat pullback to rewrite the result as the same relation for the Gysin images (proof lines 7505-7523).
Conclude by uniqueness: the characterisation identifies those classes with the caps of the Chern classes of the restricted bundle (proof lines 7524-7525).
proof_roadmap: Apply the Gysin map and rewrite (proof lines 7505-7523).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that capping with a Chern class commutes with the Gysin map attached to a Cartier divisor (statement lines 7484-7493, tag 02SL-adjacent). The proof records the characterising relation for the classes obtained by capping with the Chern classes, applies the Gysin map to that relation using the fibre product of the projective bundles, uses compatibility of the Gysin map with the cap with a first Chern class and with flat pullback to rewrite the result, and identifies it by the uniqueness in the characterisation. The rewriting through the Gysin compatibilities is the substance, so the claim is H2.
